cards.title: Google DeepMind Announces Gemini 4 Argon: Frontier Model with 1M Output Tokens and 77.9% on DeepSWE
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI/ML engineer, Gemini 4 Argon represents a major frontier model release with directly relevant capabilities: SOTA software engineering benchmarks, massive output context, and real internal deployments at Google scale.
cards.summary: Gemini 4 Argon launches in limited access via Google's Fairwind Program. It sets a new SOTA on DeepSWE v1.1 at 77.9% and leads the Vals Index across finance, coding, legal, and tax. Output token limit expands to 1M (up from 64K). Pricing: $2/M input, $10/M output, 95% off cached inputs. Internal use cases include C++→Rust migration (800K+ lines), memory optimization freeing 300 TiB across Google data centers, and quantum algorithm optimization beating a published baseline by 40%.

cards.title: Google DeepMind's SynthID Bio Watermarks AI-Generated Proteins That Remain Detectable After Physical Synthesis
cards.why_it_matters: A technically novel safety primitive at the intersection of AI and biosecurity — the watermark survives the digital-to-physical transition, which is a meaningful capability advance relevant to AI safety and responsible deployment research.
cards.summary: SynthID Bio embeds imperceptible watermarks into AI-designed proteins by subtly guiding amino acid choice (sequences) and adjusting atomic coordinates (3D structures). Wet-lab testing across three target proteins (VEGF-A, SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD, PD-L1) showed watermarked binders matched unwatermarked hit rate, binding affinity, and sequence diversity. For structure prediction, a small portion of AlphaFold 3's diffusion network is fine-tuned to embed watermarks natively into model weights with near-perfect detectability.

cards.title: Open TTS Leaderboard Launches Objective, Multilingual Evaluation for 8K+ Hugging Face TTS Models
cards.why_it_matters: If you work with or evaluate TTS systems, this leaderboard offers a fast, reproducible, objective alternative to slow arena-style voting — covering open-weight models that arenas systematically underrepresent.
cards.summary: Hugging Face's Open TTS Leaderboard evaluates models on WER/CER (via Qwen3 ASR), batched inference speed (RTFx) and streaming latency (TTFA) on H200, and speaker similarity (WavLM cosine similarity). Evaluation drops from weeks to hours. Kokoro-82M, Supertonic-3, and fishaudio/s2-pro lead on English WER. Multilingual and voice-cloning splits included; human preference ranking is explicitly not replaced.

cards.title: Ranking-PE: AUROC-Optimized Prompt Evolution for Imbalanced Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
cards.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to anyone doing prompt optimization or RLHF-adjacent work on imbalanced datasets — it shows accuracy-based objectives can actively harm ranking quality in high-stakes settings, and offers a drop-in fix.
cards.summary: Ranking-PE replaces per-instance correctness cells in prompt-evolution score matrices with pairwise-ordering cells over (positive, negative) pairs, whose column average equals empirical AUROC by the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney identity. Applied to MIMIC across three diseases, it beats accuracy-based prompt evolution by +5.8 AUROC pp on fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B and +16.2 pp on MedGemma-4B, at no extra model calls. Ablations show a medical-grade visual backbone is a prerequisite that prompt search alone cannot substitute.

cards.title: SCAPO: Semifactual Stability Improves Token-Level Credit Assignment in GRPO, Gains 5.63 pp on AIME
cards.why_it_matters: A technically grounded improvement to GRPO's credit assignment — directly relevant if you work on RL post-training for reasoning, addressing a concrete spurious-correlation failure mode with measurable gains.
cards.summary: SCAPO identifies that GRPO assigns uniform outcome-derived advantage to all tokens, potentially reinforcing sensitivity to task-irrelevant prompt features. It measures token probability drift under semifactual interventions (same problem, same answer, varied surface form) and downweights advantages for high-drift tokens in early training. On Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-1.7B-Base, SCAPO improves AIME 2024–2026 accuracy over GRPO by 5.63 and 4.17 percentage points respectively, with gains on most math and all OOD benchmarks tested.

cards.title: Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text Gains Were Largely Explained by Word-Duration Shortcuts, Not Brain Signals
cards.why_it_matters: A critical reproducibility finding for anyone following BCI or neural decoding research — it reframes a reported accuracy result and shows that a simple architectural fix yields genuinely stronger decoding.
cards.summary: The authors show that overlapping fixed-length windows in d'Ascoli et al. (2025) implicitly encode inter-word timing, allowing networks to guess words from duration statistics rather than brain activity: synthetic (brain-free) signals reach 22.0% balanced accuracy vs. 22.3% on real recordings. Processing each window independently eliminates the shortcut. The resulting SimpleB2T achieves 36.6% WER with five observations per word on perceived speech, approaching past invasive decoding results.

cards.title: ViTeX-Bench: First Real-Video Benchmark for Scene Text Editing with 387 Videos and 13 Metrics
cards.why_it_matters: Relevant to researchers in video generation/editing or multimodal evaluation — provides a reproducible evaluation framework for a gap where general video metrics fail to capture text-specific correctness.
cards.summary: ViTeX-Bench comprises 387 real-world 720p videos with text-region masks and editing instructions across three evaluation axes: text correctness, visual/temporal quality, and edit locality, measured by 13 metrics. A 157-video frozen evaluation split supports fair comparison. The released ViTeX-Edit-14B achieves CharAcc 0.688, the highest among evaluated video-native editors, with motion-aligned glyph-video conditioning. Eight baselines tested; accurate text, temporal stability, and scene preservation remain difficult to achieve simultaneously.
